title: Authentication (passkeys), onboarding & training profile, production cutover
steps:
AUTHENTICATION — strictly private, single owner (PRD §13; ADR docs/adr/0006: accept it and update it with what you actually build). Read src/hooks.server.ts, src/lib/server/env.ts, src/lib/server/auth/ (scaffold), docs/architecture.md, docs/deployment.md first.

Build passkey (WebAuthn) authentication inside the app with established libraries only — @simplewebauthn/server and @simplewebauthn/browser (latest) — no hand-rolled crypto or protocol code. Use node:crypto only for randomness and hashing of opaque tokens.

Requirements:
- Data (drizzle migration via pnpm db:generate): owner account (exactly one may exist), passkey credentials (credential id, public key, counter, transports, device type/backed-up flags, user-chosen nickname, created/last-used), sessions (store only a SHA-256 hash of the opaque random session token; created, last seen, expires, user agent summary, revoked), recovery codes (10 single-use codes, stored hashed — the codes are high-entropy so SHA-256 is fine; used_at), WebAuthn challenges (short-lived, single-use, bound to purpose), auth events/audit log (sign-in success/failure, passkey added/removed, recovery used, setup completed) and DB-backed rate limiting for every auth endpoint (no Redis).
- First-run setup: a one-time setup link `/setup?token=…`. The server reads OWNER_SETUP_TOKEN_HASH (hex SHA-256 of the token) from the environment; compare with timingSafeEqual. Setup is only possible while no owner/passkey exists; after the first passkey is registered the setup route returns 404 forever. Registration shows the 10 recovery codes exactly once with copy/download, requires explicit acknowledgement. Add OWNER_SETUP_TOKEN_HASH to the zod env schema (optional in dev/test; document it) and a script `pnpm auth:setup-token` that prints a fresh random token and its hash (for the tech lead to set on Vercel).
- Sign-in with a passkey (discoverable credentials / conditional UI where supported, plus a button). Recovery: sign in with a recovery code, which then forces registering a new passkey; used codes are burned; codes can be regenerated from settings (shows new set once).
- Passkey management in Profile → Security: list, rename, add another passkey, remove (never the last one). Session management: list active sessions (current marked), revoke one, sign out everywhere else, sign out.
- Sessions: cookie `__Host-session` (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/) in production; on plain-http localhost the Secure/__Host- prefix cannot be used, so derive cookie name/flags from the origin protocol. Sliding expiry (e.g. 30 days, refreshed at most once per day), absolute max (e.g. 90 days). Revoked/expired sessions rejected. Rotate the session id on sign-in and recovery.
- RP ID / expected origin: production must be exactly https://coach.nikocruz.com (rpID coach.nikocruz.com). Preview deployments use their own host (VERCEL_URL / request URL) and must never accept assertions for the production RP. Local dev/test: localhost. Derive this in one audited module with unit tests.
- Deny by default in hooks.server.ts: every route requires a session except an explicit allow-list (landing/sign-in page, /setup, auth API endpoints, /api/health, static/immutable assets, manifest, service worker, robots, /offline prerender). Unauthenticated page requests redirect to sign-in (with a safe same-origin return path); unauthenticated /api/* requests return 401 JSON. /api/vitals and /api/client-errors require a session. Keep the existing cross-site POST guard and verify CSRF for form actions and JSON endpoints (Origin check).
- The landing page (/) becomes the sign-in screen (premium, intentional — this is the first thing the owner sees). Signed-in users hitting / go to /today.
- Sign-out clears everything the device holds for the account: Cache Storage entries other than the current versioned shell cache, any IndexedDB databases, session cookie; consider the Clear-Site-Data header but do not wipe device preferences unless intended — document the choice.
- ENABLE_TEST_ROUTES must be impossible in production (env validation already guards — verify and extend). For WebKit e2e (no virtual authenticator), add a test-only route behind ENABLE_TEST_ROUTES that mints a session for the owner; Chromium e2e must perform REAL WebAuthn ceremonies via the CDP WebAuthn virtual authenticator (WebAuthn.enable + addVirtualAuthenticator, ctap2, internal, resident keys, user verification) for setup, sign-in, adding a second passkey, recovery-code sign-in and sign-out. Add a shared Playwright fixture/storageState so every existing e2e spec runs authenticated; keep tests independent.
- Security headers/CSP must still pass; @simplewebauthn/browser must load only on auth/security screens (keep the initial-JS budget ≤ 60 KB gzip on every route; run pnpm budgets).
- Tests: unit (RP/origin derivation, token hashing, recovery code format/consumption, cookie options), integration against real Postgres (services: setup-once, sign-in counter update, session expiry/revocation/rotation, recovery burn, rate limits), e2e (above + every app route redirects when signed out, every /api/* except allow-list returns 401 — enumerate routes from the filesystem so new routes are covered automatically).
- Docs: docs/security.md (threat model, flows, storage, cookies, CSRF, rate limits, what is and isn't protected), update ADR 0006, architecture, environment (new vars), testing, deployment (owner setup procedure). List in your summary every hosted env var the tech lead must set.

ONBOARDING & TRAINING PROFILE (PRD §2, §3; read them carefully). Build on the authenticated app from step 1.

Data model (drizzle migration; extensible, NOT weightlifting-only): athlete profile (name, units, birth year optional, body weight + history, nutrition phase bulk/cut/maintenance/recomp, weight target); goals — multiple concurrent, each typed event | general, with discipline(s), priority order (explicit rank; the coach must know which goal wins), status, and type-specific fields (event: event type, date, weight class optional, target performance, constraints; general: what to improve + how progress is measured); discipline experience per discipline (powerlifting, Olympic weightlifting, general strength, hypertrophy/bodybuilding, running, half-marathon/marathon prep, Muay Thai, general athletic performance, custom) with level/years/current frequency; strength baselines per lift — OPTIONAL, each with value + unit + kind measured | estimated + date + source (tested / e1RM from a set with reps+RPE) — never treat estimated as measured; running ability (recent race times by distance, easy pace optional, weekly volume); Muay Thai frequency/experience; equipment & facilities (gym type, available equipment list, home equipment); injuries/limitations/movements to avoid (with body area, severity, notes, active flag); exercise likes/dislikes; schedule & availability (days/week, which days, preferred times, session length, constraints, current commitments per discipline e.g. Muay Thai classes Tue/Thu). Everything versioned enough that later milestones can reason about changes (updated_at at minimum; consider history tables for body weight and goals).

Services + repositories with zod validation shared between client forms and server; all writes through services (the coach agent in M5 will call the same services).

UI (iPhone-first, premium, dark-first; reuse and extend the design system — no generic forms):
- Onboarding flow after first sign-in when the profile is incomplete: welcome → goals (asks: specific event / general goal / multiple goals; supports adding several and ordering priority by drag or up/down) → experience per selected discipline → strength baselines with the explicit, reassuring option 'I don't know my 1RM' that explains week-1 RPE-based baseline establishment (all 1RM fields can stay blank) → running/Muay Thai specifics when relevant → equipment → injuries & limitations → exercise preferences → schedule & availability → body & nutrition → review & confirm. Progress indicator, back/forward, save-as-you-go (resume where left), skippable optional steps, good empty/loading/error states, numeric inputs use the NumberStepper/keyboard-appropriate inputs, 44px+ targets, works one-handed.
- Profile screen: every section above editable later (dedicated edit screens/sheets), plus Security (from step 1) and device preferences.
- Today screen: until onboarding is complete, a designed 'finish setting up' state; after, a summary of goals/priorities and schedule (no programming yet — that is M3).
- Accessibility: axe passes in dark and light for every new screen; labels, errors announced.
- Performance: keep route JS within budget (lazy-load heavy step components if needed); no layout shift; measure with pnpm budgets and the perf e2e project.

Tests: integration round-trips for profile, goals (priorities reorder), experience, baselines (measured vs estimated preserved), schedule, equipment, injuries, preferences; e2e: complete onboarding leaving EVERY 1RM blank → profile persists across reload and in the DB; edit a goal and reorder priorities from Profile; resume a half-finished onboarding after reload; screenshots of every onboarding step saved for review (test-results/screens/...). Update docs (data model in architecture.md, milestones status).

PRODUCTION CUTOVER & HARDENING. This milestone's PR is the one that turns production on (docs/deployment.md, docs/milestones.md M2 criterion 6). Do these in the repo only (the tech lead handles hosted settings):
- Remove the production guards: vercel.json `git.deploymentEnabled.main: false` and the production skip in scripts/vercel-ignore-build.sh (keep the ignore step only if it still has a purpose; otherwise remove it and update scripts/vercel-ignore-build.test.ts accordingly — the build-command tests must stay).
- Add .github/workflows/post-deploy-smoke.yml triggered by `deployment_status` (state success, environment Production) that checks https://coach.nikocruz.com: GET /api/health → 200 with db up; GET / → 200 sign-in page; GET /today unauthenticated → redirect to sign-in; GET /api/vitals unauthenticated POST → 401; security headers present. No secrets needed. Validate with actionlint if available.
- Re-audit the deny-by-default guard against every route in src/routes (a unit/e2e check that fails when a new route is not classified as public or protected).
- Self-review the auth code like a security reviewer (OWASP ASVS L2 auth/session sections as a checklist): document findings and fixes in docs/security.md.
- Update docs/deployment.md: production is on; the owner's one-time setup procedure (open https://coach.nikocruz.com/setup?token=<token from the tech lead>, register the passkey on the iPhone, store recovery codes); rollback; what to do if the passkey is lost (recovery codes; last resort: tech lead resets the owner via a documented script that requires direct DB access — implement `pnpm auth:reset-owner` that refuses to run unless explicitly confirmed and DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED is set).
- Update docs/milestones.md statuses and README.
- Run the full local gate (check, lint, unit, integration, both builds, budgets, e2e) and fix anything red. In your summary list exactly which hosted env vars must exist in Production and Preview before merge.
acceptance: Passkey auth works end to end with established libraries (no hand-rolled crypto): one-time setup link (token hash from env, constant-time compare, setup impossible once a passkey exists), sign-in, add/rename/remove passkeys (never the last), 10 single-use hashed recovery codes shown once (sign-in with a code burns it and forces new-passkey registration; regeneration works), session list/revoke/sign-out-everywhere — proven by Playwright on Chromium performing REAL WebAuthn ceremonies through the CDP virtual authenticator (no auth bypass in Chromium tests).

Deny by default: with no session, every app page redirects to sign-in (safe same-origin return path) and every /api/* endpoint except the documented allow-list (auth endpoints, /api/health) returns 401 — verified by a test that enumerates routes from src/routes so unclassified new routes fail the build; /api/vitals and /api/client-errors require a session.

Sessions and CSRF are sound: opaque random tokens stored only as hashes; cookie HttpOnly + SameSite=Lax + Secure/__Host- on https; sliding + absolute expiry; rotation on sign-in/recovery; revoked/expired rejected; cross-site state-changing requests rejected for form actions and JSON endpoints; DB-backed rate limiting on every auth endpoint; RP ID/origin derivation unit-tested (production exactly coach.nikocruz.com; previews and localhost isolated).

Onboarding supports event / general / multiple concurrent goals with explicit priority ranking, experience per discipline, OPTIONAL 1RMs with measured vs estimated (+ date/source) distinguished, running and Muay Thai specifics, equipment, injuries/limitations, exercise likes/dislikes, schedule & availability, body weight and nutrition phase — and everything is editable later from Profile.

Playwright: signed in, complete onboarding leaving every 1RM blank; the profile persists across reload and in Postgres; a half-finished onboarding resumes after reload; editing a goal and reordering priorities from Profile persists.

Integration tests against real Postgres round-trip profile, goals with priorities, experience, baselines (measured vs estimated preserved), running/Muay Thai data, equipment, injuries, preferences and schedule through the services with validation errors for bad input.

Screens are premium and intentional on an iPhone viewport (judge screenshots of sign-in, setup, recovery codes, every onboarding step, Profile, Security, Today pre/post onboarding) with designed empty, loading and error states; axe reports zero WCAG A/AA violations in dark and light for every new screen.
Sign-out clears the device's account data (session cookie, Cache Storage other than the versioned shell, IndexedDB) — verified by e2e.

Production cutover is ready in the repo: vercel.json production guards removed, post-deploy smoke workflow added (actionlint clean), deny-by-default route classification test in place, owner setup + lost-passkey procedures documented (with a guarded `pnpm auth:reset-owner`), docs/security.md written (threat model + ASVS-style self-review), ADR 0006 accepted, env vars documented; no secrets committed.

All gates pass locally: pnpm check and lint (0 errors), unit, integration, pnpm build and build:node, pnpm budgets (initial JS ≤ 60 KB gzip on every route, @simplewebauthn/browser not in non-auth routes), full pnpm test:e2e including the perf project; all work committed on feat/m2-auth-onboarding with Conventional Commits.
